template_id: "TEMPORAL_HIERARCHY_ARCH_PE_001"

name: "Temporal Hierarchy of Architectural Prediction Error — How PE Events at Different Timescales Integrate into Architectural Experience"

structural_pattern: >
  Architectural experience generates prediction errors across a
  hierarchy of timescales spanning seven orders of magnitude. This
  hierarchy is not merely a catalogue — it reveals that architectural
  experience is CONSTITUTED by the integration of PE events at
  different temporal scales, just as musical experience is
  constituted by integration across beat, phrase, section, and
  movement timescales. The temporal hierarchy systematizes what
  previous templates address within their individual domains.
  
  THE SEVEN TIMESCALES:
  
  T-1: MILLISECONDS (50–500ms) — Perceptual PE.
  Contour detection and curvature PE (VF1, ~150ms), luminance
  contrast PE (L1), rapid material evaluation (T9, ~150ms implicit
  evaluation), acoustic onset PE (AX1, brainstem timing).
  These are the fastest architectural PEs — preconscious, automatic,
  and operating on every visual fixation and auditory sample.
  
  T-2: SECONDS (1–30s) — Motor and Navigational PE.
  Motor prediction during movement (TP1, step-by-step), postural
  adjustment (TP1), spatial transition at thresholds (TP2, SC3),
  isovist update as occupant moves (SC2), visual rhythm from
  column/window spacing at walking pace (VF2). This is the
  timescale of active movement through architecture — each step,
  each turn, each threshold crossing.
  
  T-3: MINUTES (1–30 min) — Promenade and Sequence PE.
  The architectural promenade (SC3), the sequence of spatial
  revelations, the emotional trajectory of moving through a
  building. ITPRA cycles at decision points (M5). Navigational
  PE at choice points (SC1). Climactic multi-modal convergence
  (M16, AX3). Subjective time expansion from PE density
  (Wittmann). This is the timescale of a building visit as a
  composed experience.
  
  T-4: HOURS (1–12 hrs) — Occupancy and Adaptation PE.
  Dynamic light changes through the day (L5), thermal drift and
  adaptive comfort adjustment (MAT2), attention fatigue and
  restoration (T25, ART), social encounter patterns (SC4).
  This is the timescale of a workday, a museum visit, or a
  day at home — where initial PE events habituate and the
  building becomes background until conditions change.
  
  T-5: DAYS TO WEEKS — Circadian and Habituation PE.
  Circadian light architecture (L2, ipRGC → SCN pathway),
  seasonal thermal adaptation (MAT2, de Dear adaptive model),
  cognitive map formation and updating (T3, SC1). Habituation
  of initially novel features; revelation of previously
  unnoticed details. The building shifts from novel to familiar,
  from foreground to background.
  
  T-6: MONTHS TO YEARS — Seasonal and Functional PE.
  Seasonal light and thermal cycles, spatial adaptation (space
  plan changes, furniture rearrangement), functional repurposing.
  Occupant's cognitive map matures; shortcuts discovered;
  previously invisible spatial logic becomes legible. The building
  reveals its temporal depth through seasonal material changes
  (deciduous planting, snow on structure, summer vs. winter light
  angles).
  
  T-7: DECADES TO CENTURIES — Aging and Cultural PE.
  Material aging and patina (TP3), shearing-layer adaptation
  (Brand), cultural layering and reinterpretation. The building
  as temporal process — acquiring fractal richness through
  weathering, spatial complexity through adaptation, cultural
  depth through continued use. This is the timescale at which
  buildings become "timeful" — carriers of history that
  occupants can read in the built fabric.
